scope.description: Five-voter cluster whose leading node is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs after a snapshot that predates the membership change; as soon as NewRaft returns, the restarted node is isolated together with one committed voter while the other three remain connected to each other. Report the rebuilt configuration, whether the restarted node becomes leader, how many votes were reachable, and whether the majority side holds a leader. Run with the flag on and off.
assumptions: The snapshot carries the three-voter bootstrap configuration, so the restarted node's rebuilt configuration is smaller than the committed one.
The isolated side holds two votes; the committed five-voter configuration requires three.
Cutting the partner off from the majority side removes the existing-leader guard that otherwise refuses the vote.
excluded: Any occurrence-rate or absence bound; a bounded observation is not a frequency estimate.
Entry-level divergence after the minority leadership, which needs a separate setup.

basis.prefix: The harness uses MakeClusterCustom(Peers 3, CommitTrackingLogs, RestoreCommittedLogs), ten Apply calls, an explicit Snapshot(), MakeClusterNoBootstrap(2) merged and two AddVoter calls, ten further Apply calls, then Shutdown and NewRaft on the same logs, stable and snapshots stores with a fresh inmem transport. Immediately after NewRaft it partitions the restarted node plus one committed voter away from the other three and reconnects only that pair, then emits multivoter_after_restart and multivoter_partition_election events carrying the mode, snapshots, restore flag, configuration indices and server counts, the leadership outcome, reachable votes, committed quorum, the majority-side leadership and both terms; no production logic is modified.
basis.responsibility: The library owns the quorum arithmetic a restarted node applies; with a stale rebuilt configuration it can decide an election that the committed configuration would refuse, which the caller cannot repair through the public API.

comparisons.description: An election on the isolated side must not produce a leader whose support is below the committed configuration's quorum; the defect prediction is that it does.
Control: with the committed configuration rebuilt the isolated side cannot reach three votes and must not produce a leader.
The same run re-checks the rebuilt configuration against the committed log; the defect prediction is the snapshot's configuration.
Control: the identical restart without the flag keeps the committed configuration.

before.description: An election on the isolated side must not produce a leader whose support is below the committed configuration's quorum; the defect prediction is that it does.
Control: with the committed configuration rebuilt the isolated side cannot reach three votes and must not produce a leader.
The same run also re-checks that the restarted node's configuration matches the committed log; the defect prediction is that it falls back to the snapshot's configuration.
Control: the identical restart without the flag keeps the committed configuration.

after.description: An election on the isolated side must not produce a leader whose support is below the committed configuration's quorum; the defect prediction is that it does.
Control: with the committed configuration rebuilt the isolated side cannot reach three votes and must not produce a leader.
The same run re-checks the rebuilt configuration against the committed log; the defect prediction is the snapshot's configuration.
Control: the identical restart without the flag keeps the committed configuration.

revision_reason: Only the comparison declaration and the result event names change: the immediate-isolation scenario now emits imv_after_restart and imv_partition_election, unique to this schedule, so each comparison sees exactly one result event and can complete. The scenario, stores, isolation timing, window and assertions are unchanged from the previous execution.
